added_Fact: [F6] For the orbit projection $q:P\to P/\mathbb R$, the quotient topology has $U$ open exactly when $q^{-1}(U)$ is open in $P$; in particular $q$ is continuous ([[def-quotient-topology]]). The moduli Definition initially specifies only an orbit set ([[def-unparametrized-morse-trajectory-moduli-space]]).
replacement_proof_step_3_1: 3.1 Translating each trajectory by its unique time $t_0$ from step 2.1 gives exactly one representative in $h^{-1}(c)$. Conversely, two representatives in the same time orbit can both lie in that slice only if their translation is zero. This is the level-representative bijection, using only the continuity and strict-decrease part of [F2]. Put $S=h^{-1}(c)$. The same equation $h(t\cdot\gamma)=c$, now with $\gamma$ varying in a chart of the entire $P$, has nonzero time derivative at every solution. By [F5] its unique hitting time $\tau(\gamma)$ is smooth locally on $P$; uniqueness patches these local functions globally. It satisfies $\tau(s\cdot\gamma)=\tau(\gamma)-s$, so $r(\gamma)=\tau(\gamma)\cdot\gamma$ is a smooth orbit-invariant map $P\to S$ restricting to the identity on $S$. Let $q:P\to P/\mathbb R$ carry the quotient topology [F6]. The induced inverse $\bar r:P/\mathbb R\to S$ is continuous: for every open $U\subseteq S$, $q^{-1}(\bar r^{-1}(U))=r^{-1}(U)$ is open, and [F6] applies. Conversely $q|_S$ is continuous, and these two maps are inverses. Thus the slice bijection is a homeomorphism for the quotient topology. Transport its smooth structure to $\mathcal M(p,q)$; its underlying topology is precisely that quotient topology, and its dimension is the one in step 2.1. Any other $c'$ strictly between the endpoint values gives the same smooth structure: the equation $h(t\cdot\gamma)=c'$ has nonzero derivative in $t$, so [F5] makes the unique hitting time smooth locally on the first slice; uniqueness patches these local times, and the smooth flow action gives mutually inverse smooth change-of-slice maps. Thus the construction and the empty case prove the full statement without Sard's theorem, an ambient regular level, or an added choice hypothesis. [F2, F3, F5, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct] ∎
